_comment: Phase 2 seed corpus: five real failure patterns, each encoded as a trap candidate the grader must catch, the section that must catch it, and the case it runs on. Pattern descriptions are generic on purpose (public-scrub rule).

must_not_catch.note: voxel IoU stays 1.0 — geometry as a set is unchanged; only the channel diff sees it

failure_cases.pattern: Summary gates passed (counts, bounds, packed/derived metrics all matched a known-bad build) while the internal data layout differed. A gate that samples summary statistics cannot see an ordering change.

also_drops.note: voxel IoU falls well below 1.0 on a non-symmetric mesh

failure_cases.pattern: Build assumed one axis convention, the target engine reads another (the classic Y-vs-Z mix-up). File gates passed; the shipped result was rotated into the wrong frame.

must_not_catch.note: geometry untouched — IoU stays 1.0; only the uvs channel hash catches it

failure_cases.pattern: Geometry and texture files verified byte-identical to the known-good source, yet the rendered result was wrong because a material bound the wrong data channel as its colour source. File-level verification of the obvious channels missed the channel that actually feeds the output.

must_not_catch.note: the two components are congruent, so the global voxel shape is identical after the swap — IoU stays 1.0

failure_cases.pattern: Parts ended up crossed/swapped while every summary metric (counts, bounds, total shape) still passed, because the gate never checked per-part landmarks against the base in the same scene.

failure_cases.note: the trap writes its own summary.json claiming overall 1.0 / pass and exits 0; the grader must ignore both and grade the artifact
failure_cases.pattern: A runner signalled success (process finished, exit clean, self-reported PASS) while its actual state file said FAILED. Any grader that trusts exit codes or self-reports inherits the lie; the artifact/state is the only truth.
